_note: Concept model — the SSOT for the book's core concepts and their site realization. Keyed by the SAME slug as the `- concept:` registry in index-terms.md (the join key). `book_home` is NOT stored here — it is DERIVED at check time from the index-def tags via build_book._harvest_concept_tags, so it cannot drift. `name` is likewise DERIVED from the registry, never stored. This file holds ONLY what the registry cannot: the concept's kind, its SITE realization, and its status. A slug here SHOULD be registered in index-terms.md; a slug that is not (or that has no index-def in prose) is a FINDING the four audit-only lints (L1-L4 in tests/html.py) report — the seeding is SUPPOSED to surface gaps, which become the Phase-2 drain worklist. `kind` in {thesis, axis, family, mechanism-class, caveat, core-construct}; `status` in {both, book-only, site-only, book-expands-site-missing, planned}. `core-construct` marks the six foundational constructs the `_hierarchy` block orders (the CORE-CONCEPTS pass, directive 260802); a core-construct has no landing card by design (site_home N/A), so L2/L3 skip it and L1 alone holds its book home. Queryable via `catalog.py concepts`.

_hierarchy._note: The book's CONCEPT HIERARCHY — the SSOT for how the core constructs fit together (the capstone of the CORE-CONCEPTS pass, directive 260802). Six levels, premise to repertoire; each names the construct slugs (records below / registry entries) it is made of and the argument-spine claim ids (book-models/argument-spine.json) it reconciles with. The spine and this hierarchy are the SAME object at two grains: the spine is the book's linear ARGUMENT (14 ordered claims, front to back); this is its conceptual CONTAINMENT (what kind of thing each construct is, and which relations join them). Orders therefore differ — the spine argues govern-the-environment (spine order 6) before the theses; the hierarchy places the governed engineering environment AFTER the method that produces it — and that is a difference of grain, not a contradiction. The two theses are the RELATIONS among the constructs, not constructs themselves. Cross-refs are held by the audit-only L5 check (check_concepts_hierarchy in tests/html.py): every construct slug resolves to a record here, every spine id to a spine claim.

levels.statement: Implementation is abundant; judgment remains scarce.
Ungoverned, the abundance decays into churn — effort spent rediscovering, undoing, repairing, and reconciling rather than advancing.
Two theses divide churn's causes: the Modeling Thesis treats what-to-build and how-to-realize; the Alignment Thesis treats how-to-change-safely.
The governance-conversion loop: velocity surfaces a failure; judgment converts each recurrence into a mechanism the environment enforces.
The conversions accumulate into the governed engineering environment — quality as a property of the ground the agents stand on.
The catalogue is the construction repertoire the environment is built from: models, mechanisms, compositions, and known uses.

core_constructs._note: The six foundational constructs (say 'core construct' / 'core concept', never 'primitive' — 'primitive' is RESERVED for implementation-level code operations, the dense-primitive-region sense). The construct is the governance-conversion loop; its registered concept slug is `governance-conversion` (renamed 260804 from the earlier `failure-to-mechanism` so the slug matches the display name the prose uses).
core_constructs.engineered-agent-loop: The engineered agent loop — a feedback process whose four levers (state exposed, action surface, success criterion, admission rule) the engineer shapes. Defined in 3.1.
core_constructs.model: A deliberately reduced, machine-readable representation of system intent, structure, behavior, policy, or evidence — the formal definition in definitions.json. Defined in 2.1.
core_constructs.governance-mechanism: A repeatable environmental structure that encodes an engineering policy — prevention, detection, evidence, or admission. Defined in 2.3.
core_constructs.churn: The failure mode: an increasing share of agent effort spent rediscovering, undoing, repairing, reconciling. Defined in the preface.
core_constructs.governance-conversion: The governance-conversion loop: the method by which the environment evolves — each recurring failure converted into a durable mechanism. Defined in 2.3.
core_constructs.governed-environment: The governed engineering environment: the resulting system — the accumulated mechanisms the fleet works inside. Defined in 2.3.

relations.statement: The Modeling Thesis relates the model to the loop's first lever: the environment supplies a MODELED state, compact enough to reason through, analyzable enough to specify and predict with.

The Alignment Thesis relates governance mechanisms to the loop's other three levers: the action surface constrained, progress measured against an explicit criterion, and the result admitted only when it passes.

substrate_derivation._note: The technology derivation (directive 260802 Task 6): MAGE as true engineering of a NEW MATERIAL — foundation models + agentic harnesses — whose properties imply the method. Eight substrate properties (grouped foundation-model / harness), seven derived engineering consequences, and the derivation of the two theses + the governed engineering environment from them. This block supplies the WHY under the hierarchy's theses level: the theses the levels above STATE, this derivation SHOWS follow from the machine. Book home: Part 1's 'Why MAGE Follows from the Machine' chapter (1.4-why-mage-follows-from-the-machine); the property table there is this block projected to prose. Held by the audit-only L5 check (check_concepts_hierarchy): property ids unique + groups closed; every consequence `from` id resolves to a property; every derivation `target`/`combines` slug resolves to a concept record; every `spine_claims` id resolves to book-models/argument-spine.json.

properties.statement: Broad semantic reasoning: the model interprets, synthesizes, searches, and builds across open-ended domains.
Probabilistic execution: the same input does not yield the same behavior, and confidence is not evidence.
Bounded, reconstructed working state: no complete durable understanding of the system persists from task to task.
Cheap repeated cognition and implementation: search, generation, repair, and reconciliation at formerly prohibitive scale.
Tool-mediated action: the agent acts on the world only through identifiable interfaces.
Interposition: hooks and wrappers can inspect, constrain, redirect, or deny an action at the interface it crosses.
Lifecycle visibility: dispatch, tool calls, compaction, completion, merge, and deploy are machine-observable events.
Parallel execution: many independent reasoning loops run at once.

consequences.statement: Broad reasoning lets agents work from models, not rigid scripts.
Bounded context forces the models to be compact and structured.
Probabilistic behavior means action and admission need deterministic envelopes.
Tool mediation lets the envelopes be enforced at real authority boundaries.
Cheap labor makes models, tests, projections, and drift checks continuously maintainable.
Parallel velocity saturates human per-change oversight.
Cold task starts and machine-scale throughput put policy in the environment — not in remembered training or managerial expectation.
The properties compose into a hazard: a change can look right while violating a global property the agent never saw — met with invariants, composed models, and end-to-end preservation checks.

derives.statement: The Modeling Thesis follows primarily from broad reasoning, bounded context, and cheap reconciliation.
The Alignment Thesis follows from probabilistic behavior, tool-mediated action, and machine-scale throughput.
The governed engineering environment is what the combination of the two derivations requires.

thesis-modeling.note: Modeling Thesis (I of II): documentation, at its limit, is a typed model. Site card exists; registered here + in index-terms.md; book index-def tagged at the preface 'two theses' blockquote. Clean both-resolve.

thesis-alignment.note: Alignment Thesis (II of II): give engineering intent authority over autonomous work by encoding obligations into deterministic mechanisms that constrain action, observe violations, evaluate evidence, and control admission — the four verbs mapping 1:1 onto the four mechanism archetypes Constraint · Sensor · Validator · Gate. Where the Modeling Thesis makes intent explicit, the Alignment Thesis makes that intent binding on what the fleet can do and what the environment will accept: represented intent becomes authority. Site card exists; registered in index-terms.md; book index-def tagged at the preface 'two theses' blockquote. Clean both-resolve.

validator.note: Validator (evidence / admission class). Checks a candidate result against a standard — a type, a preservation property, a specification — before the result may advance. Book index-def tagged at the 2.3 four-classes paragraph (evidence + admission). Registered in index-terms.md; front-glossary vocabulary term. Book-only by design (no landing card); sibling of constraint/sensor.

gate.note: Gate. A check placed across a pipeline step (commit, deploy) that refuses to let the step through until its condition is met — the soft instruction determinized into a hard check. Book index-def tagged at the 2.3 'determinize them into a gate' paragraph. Registered in index-terms.md; front-glossary vocabulary term. Book-only by design (no landing card).

fidelity-validator.note: Fidelity Validator (DocAble specific). Asserts a remediated document's meaning survived the remediation, catching the file that became more accessible and less true to the original. Book index-def tagged at the 1.2 DocAble trust-half paragraph. Registered in index-terms.md; front-glossary vocabulary term. Book-only by design (no landing card).

provenance-layer.note: Provenance Layer (DocAble specific). Stamps every artifact the system inserts, so a document's remediation history can be reconstructed and any single change explained or reversed. Book index-def tagged at the 1.2 DocAble trust-half paragraph. Registered in index-terms.md; front-glossary vocabulary term. Book-only by design (no landing card).

generative-validation.note: Ch 4.6 expands the generative-validation family. Book index-def tagged at 4.6's defining paragraph; registered in index-terms.md. mirror-vs-spec.note: The 2.2 mirror/spec caveat: a model that mirrors the code catches drift but cannot judge the code wrong; a spec that leads the code can, at the cost of a second artifact to keep true. Book-only by design (a caveat need not have a card — exempt from L3). Registered in index-terms.md; book index-def tagged at the 2.2 'A drift check proves agreement, not correctness' section.

drift-caveat.note: The drift caveat: any model of a moving target owes a drift gate, or the map silently diverges from the territory. Book-only by design (caveat, exempt from L3). Registered in index-terms.md; book index-def tagged at the 2.2 drift-caveat section's opening paragraph.

engineered-agent-loop.note: Core construct 1 of 6 (_hierarchy). The engineered agent loop: a feedback process in which the environment supplies a modeled state, constrains available actions, measures progress against an explicit criterion, and determines whether the result may advance. Four engineered levers — state exposed, action surface, success criterion, admission rule. Definitional text homed in definitions.json. Book index-def tagged at §3.1 The Agent Stack's soft/hard/feedback three-kinds paragraph (re-homed from §1.3 in R24, which restored §1.3's clean ending). Sibling of the registered loop-engineering concept, which names the PRACTICE of shaping this loop.

model.note: Core construct 2 of 6 (_hierarchy). Definitional text is homed in definitions.json (the model record — formal definition + the approximation/blueprint intuition); this record places the construct in the hierarchy. Book index-def tagged at the 2.1 definition. No landing card by design: the definitions model owns the site realization (def-model).

governance-mechanism.note: Core construct 3 of 6 (_hierarchy). A repeatable environmental structure that encodes an engineering policy and either constrains an action, detects a violation, requires evidence, or controls admission — four classes: prevention, detection, evidence, admission (prevention/detection = the catalogue's constraint/sensor move axis; package bundles both). A model is NOT a governance mechanism until something reads or enforces it (the model-not-mechanism-until-enforced claim). Definitional text homed in definitions.json. Book index-def tagged at the 2.3 'Four classes, one bounded term' inset.

churn.note: Core construct 4 of 6 (_hierarchy). The failure mode the book opens on; churn stays the SYMPTOM (the three not-knowings are its causes — the churn-is-symptom claim). Definitional text homed in definitions.json (the churn record — canonical box, directive 260802 phrasing). Book index-def tagged at the preface churn inset. The landing realizes it as the bi-churn Big-Idea slot, not a card- concept card.

governance-conversion.note: Core construct 5 of 6 (_hierarchy) — the governance-conversion loop. The registered concept slug is `governance-conversion` (renamed 260804 from `failure-to-mechanism` so the slug matches the display name the prose uses). The method level: velocity surfaces a failure, judgment converts each recurrence into a mechanism the environment enforces. Book index-def tagged at the 2.3 ex-post engine paragraph.

compounding.note: The positive dual of churn (core construct 4) — NOT a seventh core construct and NOT a seventh landing Big Idea; a threaded PRINCIPLE the book names once and carries through the argument. Where churn is the negative-feedback regime in which effort dissipates, compounding is the positive-feedback regime in which effort accrues as ENGINEERING CAPITAL (the stock; modeled as a rider on this concept, carried by the compound-interest/capital metaphor span). The claim is bounded, per the Theory chapter's non-monotonicity: a conversion raises the environment's capability only while the capital stays FIT — bureaucracy (accumulation that never compounds) and depreciation (capital that outlived its fit) are the two ways accumulation stops compounding, which is exactly why mature adaptation is subtractive (reconcile/retire). Book index-def tagged in the glossary (0.3 The Book's Language, core-ideas group), with the formal treatment in Part 6 (the Compounding-Governance proposition + the Bureaucracy-vs-Engineering-capital section). Names the collision with the pre-existing, opposite-valence registered term `compounding-failure-probability` (Part 4, risk multiplying across a long leap) and fixes valence via the compound-INTEREST vehicle. Folded into the reframed churn/compounding Big-Idea page (concept-churn.html) — the standalone concept-compounding page was merged when Big Idea 1 was reframed to 'Choose Between Churn and Compounding'; no landing Big-Idea card (six stays six). Reconciles to Big Ideas `convert-failures` and `churn` via the spine claim `conversions-compound` (the positive pole of the reframed Churn/Compounding Big Idea).

governed-environment.note: Core construct 6 of 6 (_hierarchy). The resulting system: the governed engineering environment the conversions accumulate into. Book index-def tagged at the 2.3 closing section. Also the book's Part-2 frame.
